title: Predictive Role of Self‐Esteem in Depression and General Self‐Efficacy Among College Students: A Longitudinal Cross‐Lagged Study From China
abstract: Background In higher education contexts, self‐esteem (SE) is regarded as an important psychological resource that supports the development of a positive self‐identity and the realization of individual potential among college students, ultimately facilitating improvements in educational quality. Methods This study conducted a two‐wave longitudinal survey with a 1‐year interval among 2298 Chinese college students and employed correlation analyses together with cross‐lagged panel models to examine the temporal relationships among SE, depression (DEP), and general self‐efficacy (GSE). Results Results showed that SE was inversely associated with DEP and positively associated with GSE among college students, with large effect sizes observed at both measurement waves (| r | ≥ 0.50). Furthermore, SE significantly predicted lower levels of DEP and higher levels of GSE. DEP negatively predicted SE, whereas GSE positively predicted SE. Conclusion This study provides further support for the mutual risk model linking SE and DEP and offers additional evidence for the reciprocal predictive association between SE and GSE. The findings highlight the importance of developing effective institutional strategies to promote college students′ psychological health, overall well‐being, and positive development.
